tasks.title: Set a pushed branch's upstream only when it has none
tasks.description: Omarchy session 12 queue: picked by the owner on 2026-10-01 from the findings of the Omarchy work (B3; docs/validation.md ~485-491: pushing main to a second remote moved its upstream from origin/main to lan/main). Owner decision (2026-10-01): set the upstream only when the branch has none, as Git's push.autoSetupRemote does. Branch Push (crates/git-core/src/work.rs:755-800, `WriteCommand::Push`) always passes `--set-upstream` (:795). After the existing `show-ref --verify`, read the local branch's upstream with a fixed-argument passive read (for example `for-each-ref --format=%(upstream) refs/heads/‹branch›`) and pass `--set-upstream` only when it is empty. A configuration change between that read and the push is accepted and documented: at worst an upstream added concurrently is overwritten, as today. The app's Push copy (crates/app/src/workspace.rs ~1461-1482) promises nothing about upstreams and stays unchanged; historical validation entries stay as written. Test to extend: crates/git-core/tests/workflow.rs:366 `clone_fetch_fast_forward_pull_and_non_force_push_use_local_remote`. Queue 2026-10-02 (coordinator, 2026-10-01): references checked against main. git-core only and not rendered, so it sits outside the evidence chain and needs no native, performance, package or vendor attestation.

acceptance.description: A git-core test with two local bare remotes pushes a branch whose upstream is origin/main to the second remote and asserts that the push succeeds, the second remote's branch moves, and `branch.‹name›.remote` and `branch.‹name›.merge` still name origin and refs/heads/main; it fails on origin/main.
A branch with no upstream still gets the pushed remote branch as its upstream after a successful push, and a rejected push sets none; both asserted by tests.

The upstream read follows crates/git-core/AGENTS.md's passive-read policy (fixed arguments, no optional locks, no network) and adds no write; a test asserts `--set-upstream` is passed only when the branch has no upstream.
crates/git-core/README.md:28 and docs/architecture.md:98 state the new rule, and docs/user-guide.md says a branch's first push sets its upstream and later pushes to another remote leave it.

tasks.title: Keep a focused repository tab's ring inside the strip at small text sizes
tasks.description: Coordinator follow-up of 2026-10-01 (HANDOFF "Finish-all coordinator"; docs/validation.md ~817, the #94 entry's "Not covered" note; DESIGN.md:27 "Still open: … text scales below about 0.875, where the tab strip leaves less than 3 px above and below a tab"). The repository tab strip (crates/app/src/repository_tabs.rs ~1895-1930) is `min_h(appearance::ui_size(36.))` (:1905) around the `repository-tabs` list, which keeps `appearance::button_ring_room` (appearance.rs:246, 3 px at the default ring) inside its clip as padding and gives it back through a negative margin (:1925-1926). The interface text size runs 11 to 18 pt (appearance.rs:31, default 13) and the desktop text scale 0.5 to 3.0 (:35), so `ui_scale` reaches about 0.42. Below about 0.875 the strip leaves less than the ring room above and below a tab, and because the strip is the window's first row the top of a focused tab's ring would leave the window. Decision (coordinator, 2026-10-01, delegated by the owner): the strip never leaves less than the ring room above and below a tab or close button: its minimum height is the larger of today's `ui_size(36.)` and the tallest tab or close button plus twice `button_ring_room`, so it grows by the few pixels it lacks at the smallest sizes and nothing moves where the room already fits. Reason: DESIGN.md:27 promises a whole ring, and the room can only come from the strip because it is the window's first row; shrinking the tabs would cramp their labels exactly where text is smallest, and a fixed extra padding would move the strip at the default size. Remove the tab-strip clause from DESIGN.md:27's "Still open" list. tasks.title: Part a focused worktree row's ring from the next row and give a selected row one outline
tasks.description: Coordinator follow-up of 2026-10-01 (HANDOFF, pre-existing findings of the `ring-clipping-lists` design review). The managed worktree list (crates/app/src/worktrees.rs:538-540, `managed-worktree-list`, `gap_1()`) builds each row as `Button::new(("managed-worktree-row", index)).ghost().w_full().h_auto().min_h(ui_size(36.)).px_3().py_2()` with `.selected(selected).toggled(selected)`, `.border_1()`, `.border_color(rgb(if selected { p.accent } else { p.border }))`, a `p.selected` fill when selected and `row_hover(true)`. (1) Rows stand 0.25 rem apart, measured at 3.25 px, so a focused row's ring (2 px, 1 px outside its edge) ends about 0.25 px from the next row's border and reads as touching it. (2) A selected row draws an accent border; when it is also focused, the 2 px accent ring sits 1 px outside that border, so the row reads as a double outline. Decision (coordinator, 2026-10-01, delegated by the owner): (a) rows stand apart by `appearance::button_ring_room` plus 2 px (5 px at the default ring) at every text size, so a focused row's ring keeps 2 px of the list's surface before the next row's border; (b) a selected row keeps the neutral `p.border` border and shows selection through its `p.selected` fill and its selected and toggled state, so an accent outline around a worktree row always means keyboard focus. Reason: DESIGN.md:27 gives the accent ring to keyboard focus and asks it to read whole; History, the branch chooser and the other lists mark selection with the selected surface, and neither a ring merged with a neighbour's border nor a ring stacked on an accent border reads as one clear state. #122's room in the list (`p(room).m(-room)`) stays. Tests go in `ring_room_tests` (worktrees.rs:580) or worktrees/tests.rs; `appearance::painted_button` (appearance.rs:274) reads painted fills and borders.
